finding.reasons: Shares a confirmed-malware code signature ['folderOpen curl filename:tasks.json'] | Tier-2 confirmed (bash score 5)

osm_report.threat_description:
VS Code autorun dropper. Payload in .vscode/tasks.json.
Outbound: fetch-and-run. It downloads code from vscode-helper171-ruby.vercel.app and executes it (.vscode/tasks.json).
Runs automatically when the folder is opened in VS Code (hidden folderOpen task that fetches and runs a remote script).
Matches PolinRider / Contagious Interview (DPRK): fake-recruiter coding tasks that run a downloader when opened in VS Code. Payload host: vscode-helper171-ruby.vercel.app.
Campaign GW-C-498a0aeb: one of 81 confirmed repos across 69 accounts sharing the dropper URL shape settings/{os}?flag=. Payload served from 18 distinct hosts, including default-configuration-sandy.vercel.app, default-configuration.vercel.app, isvalid-regions.vercel.app, vscode-bootstrapper.vercel.app, vscode-config-settings.vercel.app.
Attribution: the tradecraft is consistent with North Korea, but a single signal is a lead rather than an attribution, so we do not attribute it on this evidence alone. Signals: Delivery vector matches Contagious-Interview tradecraft: vscode-folderopen-autorun, dprk-dropper-path-shape.
Found by GitHub code search for a confirmed malware signature: folderOpen curl filename:tasks.json.
Confirmed by static analysis; the code was read, never executed.
osm_report.payload_description:
Malicious payload found in: .vscode/tasks.json
- Outbound: fetch-and-run. It downloads code from vscode-helper171-ruby.vercel.app and executes it (.vscode/tasks.json).
- .vscode/tasks.json: VS Code task with runOn: folderOpen; runs the moment the folder is opened, no install or click needed
- Attacker hosts: vscode-helper171-ruby.vercel.app
